clue.text: It's up to a drinker to reform: it takes its toll

indicators.note: to reform something is to make it over in a new shape, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A temperance campaigner insists a heavy drinker must sort himself out, since booze takes its toll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes its toll' reads as harm done by drink; literally it is a road that charges a toll.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike road was a highway with a gate where travellers paid a toll for its upkeep.

clue.text: Priest-like, put out having to back speedier process

indicators.note: to back is to move in reverse, so the assembled string is read from end to start

parts.note: short for Reverend, a priest's title
as means like, as in 'white as snow'
to emit is to put out or give off

explanation.surface: Someone tells a clergyman-like figure to stop and reverse, as if a sermon has been extinguished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priest-like' looks like one hyphenated adjective, but it splits into a priest and a word for like.
explanation.definitionFit: A time-saver is any method or device that gets a job done faster, which is a speedier process.

clue.text: About right to give another prize back

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to re-award is to award a prize again
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A judging panel asks whether it is right to hand out a second award retrospectively.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter for right sits inside the word for awarding again, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearward is an adjective or adverb meaning towards the rear, a synonym of back.

clue.text: One with attitude is a problem

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone striking an attitude or pose to impress

explanation.surface: Someone with a stroppy attitude is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attitude' suggests rudeness, but it is also the old word for a bodily posture struck deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser both strikes attitudes to show off and, separately, is a tricky question that baffles.

clue.text: Republican slogan getting a touch of improvement

definitions.text: Republican slogan getting a touch of improvement

parts.note: surface reading: an anti-monarchist rallying cry denouncing royalty
setter's reading: a disease once believed cured when a monarch touched the sufferer

explanation.surface: An anti-royal chant is being given a slight polish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a slogan the words say royals are wicked; but it is also the old name for scrofula, which the monarch's touch was supposed to heal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrofula was called this because English and French monarchs ceremonially touched sufferers to cure them.

clue.text: Animals said to have a twisted proboscis?

indicators.note: said means the words are judged by how they are pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: wry means twisted and a proboscis is a nose

explanation.surface: A whimsical description of creatures whose snouts are bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the animal's horned snout makes a crooked-nose pun plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoceroses are large horned mammals of Africa and Asia, plainly animals.

clue.text: Before Beth, this drink at pub

parts.note: ale is a beer
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink at the pub before meeting a friend called Beth.
explanation.walkthrough: Beth looks like a woman's name but is the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, so it comes immediately before beth.

clue.text: Run in to film imaginary line

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter for run goes within the next word

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
pic is informal for a picture, a film

explanation.surface: A director rushes off to shoot a movie about something make-believe.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are notional circles of latitude drawn on maps, not physical lines.

clue.text: Pilots finally wait for such a clear sky

definitions.note: describes the sky rather than naming it: an adjective for it

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of pilots
to tarry is to linger or wait

explanation.surface: Aviators wait patiently for good visibility before taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a cloudless night sky is full of visible stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear night sky shows its stars, so it is studded with them, which is what the adjective conveys.

clue.text: Sport and business qualification, a Caribbean speciality

parts.note: RU is rugby union
Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A list of credentials for a Caribbean college: games, a management degree and a local specialism.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rum, the obvious Caribbean speciality, but the answer is a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a dance that originated in Cuba, an island of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Imogen's in hospital clinic twice after initially sick feeling

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the doubled clinic
after places the doubled clinic behind the first letter rather than before it
initially points to the start of the word, keeping only its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of sick
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
the setter Imogen is, contracted to I'm
the clinic repeated

explanation.surface: The setter describes visiting two hospital departments after feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by name, so Imogen's means I am, contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or emotion, an equivalent of a feeling.

clue.text: Conflict involving Royal Mail since mid-century?

parts.note: Royal Mail is the British postal service
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A dispute about the postal service has rumbled on since the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: A conflict involving the Royal Mail is a war about the post; the question mark flags that the definition only works for the 20th century, after 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: The period after the Second World War began in the middle of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Dummy is very different

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
other means different

explanation.surface: A mannequin or fool turns out to be quite unlike what was expected.
explanation.walkthrough: A dummy here is the rubber teat given to babies, called a pacifier in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's dummy is also called a soother because sucking on it calms the infant.

clue.text: Train weapon on path to garage and get shot

parts.note: to cover someone is to keep a gun aimed at them
a drive is the private road up to a house and its garage

explanation.surface: A gunman aims along the driveway and someone gets shot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a cover drive is an attacking stroke hit through the off side past the cover fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a batting stroke, and a cricket stroke is called a shot.

clue.text: Buries urn sadly in city park

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are put into disorder

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A mourner inters a loved one's ashes in an urban green space.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'the country in the city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rus in urbe describes an illusion of countryside within a town, such as a large urban park.

clue.text: Cross yard, having had dinner, to go back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yard
to have fed is to have eaten

explanation.surface: Someone walks across the yard after dinner and then returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is not a verb of movement here but of opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross someone is to oppose or thwart them, the same as defying them.

clue.text: Overdue an unravelling of struggle

indicators.note: an unravelling pulls threads apart and loose, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A late-arriving collapse of a hard fight, like a knitted garment coming apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to strive hard, an effortful attempt like a struggle.

clue.text: Quickly produce one outstandingly attractive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make something fast and without fuss, a phrasal verb
second meaning: a stunning person, informally

explanation.surface: A fashion designer rushes out a dazzling creation.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock out a report is to dash it off; a knockout is a person of striking good looks.

clue.text: Issue drinks, perhaps not very dry

indicators.note: not means leave out, so the letter for very is dropped

parts.note: to serve drinks is to hand them out
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A bartender hands out drinks that are only slightly dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very dry' reads as a wine description, but 'not very' strips a letter instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere is a literary word for withered or parched, synonymous with dry.

clue.text: Using spades, clear out some euphorbia

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
to purge is to clear out

explanation.surface: A gardener digs out a patch of euphorbia with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: The spades look like garden tools but are the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurges are plants of the genus Euphorbia, so a spurge is an example of one.

clue.text: Seaside walks involving sand, please

indicators.note: to involve is literally to wind or roll up together, so the letters get entangled

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A beachgoer asks for strolls along the shore with sand underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Esplanades are long level promenades, typically along a seafront, where people stroll.

clue.text: Was relieved to get through second round in a bit of a dash

definitions.text: in a bit of a dash

indicators.note: to get through something is to pass inside it, so one piece goes between the others

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
informal for having urinated
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An athlete is relieved to scrape through the second round of a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: A dash is a sprint in the surface, but in the definition it is short for dashboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The speedometer is a gauge on a car's dashboard, so it is found on a bit of the dash.

clue.text: It must be Susan's series of lies

parts.note: 'tis is the old contraction of it is
Sue is the short form of Susan

explanation.surface: Someone insists that an item must belong to Susan, who has been telling fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a tissue of lies' gives the definition a whole web of falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: A tissue of lies is an idiom for an interwoven fabric of untruths, so tissue alone stands for the series.

clue.text: In social gathering no female affected charm

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for female is removed

parts.note: a function is a formal social event
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: At a party with no women present, someone turns on false charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction can mean an exaggerated, oily earnestness or suavity, a pretended charm.

clue.text: Crowd caught by sudden surge

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a rush is a sudden surge

explanation.surface: A throng is caught up in a sudden push forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A crush is a dense mass of people packed together, a throng.

clue.text: One digs the best guitar

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best
axe is musicians' slang for a guitar

explanation.surface: A rock fan says they really like the finest guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' in the surface is slang for likes; in the definition it is literal excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickaxe is a heavy tool for breaking and digging ground, so it is one that digs.

clue.text: Strong position of very minor debtor?

parts.note: P is a penny, a tiny sum
one who owes

explanation.surface: A wry comment on how much clout someone with a tiny debt has.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsy: someone owing only a penny is the most minor of debtors.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in power is holding authority, a position of strength.

clue.text: Food, wages, and a small retainer

parts.note: grub is slang for food
screw is old British slang for pay

explanation.surface: A modest servant is paid in meals, wages and a little fee.
explanation.walkthrough: A retainer looks like a household servant or fee, but here it is something that holds parts in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub screw is a small headless set screw used to retain a part, such as a knob on a shaft.

clue.text: Flock following duck, back in the day

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the flock is placed after the duck

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
a fold is a flock of sheep or a congregation

explanation.surface: Sheep trailing behind a duck, as farms used to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Of old is an idiom for in former times, like the informal back in the day.

clue.text: Shredder in capital office building

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a kitchen tool that shreds food
second meaning: the nickname of the Leadenhall Building, a wedge-shaped London skyscraper

explanation.surface: A paper-shredding machine sits in a corporate headquarters in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Leadenhall Building in the City of London is nicknamed for its sloping wedge shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheese grater shreds cheese, and the tower's tapering profile earned it the same name.
